To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) we developed a multilayer network model to integrate genomic and chemical data for drug repositioning in neglected diseases, 2) we showed that our model outperforms classic methods for prioritization, and 3) our model is able to propose new hypotheses for orphan compounds that were validated in the literature post-facto.
a multilayer network graph that combines chemical and genomic information from different organisms is an effective approach for guiding the identification of drug candidates in neglected diseases.

we developed a novel network-based strategy for prioritization of candidate drug targets and bioactive molecules in neglected pathogen genomes and we showed that it outperformed other approaches in a cross validation study and provided additional insights in the prioritization of bioactive molecules.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a novel computational strategy for the prioritization of new targets and orphan compounds in neglected diseases.
the development of a network-based approach to guide drug repositioning in the field of neglected diseases.
the development of an integrative computational model to guide drug discovery and repositioning for neglected pathogens.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the network model presented here is a useful tool to guide the process of drug repositioning in neglected diseases, and that its application can be extended to other problems of drug discovery and development.
the network model we developed provides a novel framework for prioritization of drug targets and repositioning of drugs in neglected diseases, and can be used as a tool in drug discovery.
this approach can help in the prioritization of new target proteins and bioactive compounds in the context of neglected diseases.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the network model we present in this work is a powerful tool for prioritizing candidate targets in neglected pathogens and for suggesting new targets for bioactive molecules that are not yet fully characterized.

we developed a novel integrative model to prioritize and suggest candidate targets in neglected pathogenic organisms based on the information contained in a multilayer network model that takes advantage of protein-protein and protein-chemical relations across different organisms.

we developed a novel network-based approach to prioritize drug targets in neglected diseases, which can be applied to any organism for which a network model can be constructed, and which is based on the information contained in a multilayered graph.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a network approach to integrate genomic and chemical data can help to prioritize and guide new drug discovery efforts, especially for neglected diseases.

a network-based approach to integrate information from different species and different types of data can be successfully used to prioritize new drug targets and suggest new drug repurposing strategies for neglected diseases.

the network model can help to prioritize and suggest new targets for compounds that were not previously known to bind to a specific protein and also can suggest new compounds for a target of interest.
